survivingClaim: No selector found. chi = 1 is in Helson's exceptional set E (pole at 1); RH is the statement 1 not in E_zero. E and E_zero are tail, flow-invariant, H-invariant, null and dense. E is comeagre (proved in the result); E_zero is comeagre (proved in the referee report, through non-continuation at s = 1 for generic chi, not through zeros). No closed set or G_delta contains the good set and misses E, and no rotation-invariant class separates chi = 1. The twin's drifted product measure is singular to Haar for 1/2 <= beta_0 < 0.975 and plants a simple zero at beta_0 when beta_0 > 1/2; equivalence to Haar excludes strip zeros and poles; zeta is the Dirac case. A property that holds at chi = 1 cannot be both tail and fail for finite modifications: strip zeros are a tail datum, the functional equation a one-orbit datum. Exact bounded discrepancy is not tail (Omega(log x) for chi(2) = -1, with corrected identity S(n) - n/3 = (2/3) sum (-1)^k b_k(n)); it names chi = 1 by Klurman / Klurman-Mangerel (recalled, not opened). H^2 cyclicity holds for every chi. Orbit genericity for log|zeta| is unconditional and density-only. The Mertens, half-plane outer and band-limited window forms are each equivalent to zero-freeness. The band-gap identity (Prop. 6) is correct, confirmed by independent code on zeta(s+a)zeta(s-a) and DH to about 1e-7; DH and zeta(s+a)zeta(s-a) both satisfy it, so it separates no control. No statement about zeros of zeta is established and no bound moves.
obstruction: chi = 1 lies in Helson's exceptional set E (pole at 1); E and E_zero are tail, flow-invariant, null, dense and comeagre, so no closed set, G_delta or rotation-invariant class contains the good set and misses E. A property holding at chi = 1 cannot be both tail-measurable and fail for finite modifications: strip zeros are a tail datum, the functional equation a one-orbit datum. Every every-window statistic that sorts E_zero correctly (Mertens sum, half-plane outer, band-limited window mean) is equivalent to zero-freeness. The band-gap identity for window means of log|F| holds for DH and E_a as well.
controlsThatDefeat: finite modifications of zeta (same tail class; defeat any tail-measurable property)
